history.summary: grid 2.0 — mobile-first, intrinsic auto mode, spans declared. The three 1.x defects each die with a named regression: the 640/641 range pair's fractional dead zone (640.5px now lands in the sm tier — min-width floors on the canon), the forced ≤640 collapse (the blanket [data-cols]/[data-span] presence selectors are gone; unsuffixed data-cols holds at every width, spans are never crushed, and collapsing is authored: data-cols="1" data-cols-md="2" data-cols-lg="4"), and source-order dependence — the one the task demanded beyond stack's 0.8-03 precedent. Tier precedence is encoded in SPECIFICITY: each tier block repeats [data-ui="grid"] once more than the tier below (base (0,2,0) → xl (0,6,0)), so a bundler that reorders or splits blocks cannot change which tier wins; asserted structurally per selector and behaviorally by resolving five probe ladders identically against the shipped, reversed, and selector-sorted rule orders. The cascade machinery moved to a new shared pure-function helper (tests/helpers/css-cascade.ts, generalized from stack.test.ts: component name a parameter, viewport per call instead of a window.matchMedia mock — which is what makes the reorder proof possible), consumed by grid.test.ts (28 tests) and by stats-dashboard's new test resolving the authored metrics attributes through grid.css itself (1→2→4 incl. the dead zone; suite 25→26). Feature: data-cols="auto" → repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, var(--grid-min)), 1fr)); data-min is an enum prop over rem steps 8|12|16|20|24 whose rules only re-declare --grid-min, the 16rem default sitting on the base rule at (0,1,0) so the override is specificity-safe too; auto is a full cols value so every tier accepts it; the media-free promise asserted the strong way (the WINNING rule at every probe width has media: null). Declared everything: cols/gap responsive (gap now 0–16 matching stack; declared default honestly 4→0 — no bare-grid gap rule ever existed; previews' hitherto-dead data-gap="3" now resolves), span and scroll under props — scroll keeps its 0.x phone-strip meaning re-expressed mobile-first (snap strip below sm, restored to a grid from sm up by the boosted tier rules). Manifest 2.0.0 breaking entry with both migration recipes. Grid-vocabulary consumers updated in the commit: stats-dashboard's two KPI rows + manifest template/slot description, dashboard-shell's two content grids, stat.html's example row — all pixel-identical at the capture viewport, so visual baselines survive; pricing/feature-grid/key-value only borrowed the attribute NAMES for their own vocabularies and are 0.8-09's sweep. Bindings regenerated (LGrid: auto in the union, colsSm…Xl/gapSm…Xl reusing base unions, scroll?: boolean; codegen snapshots updated), skill + registry-index regenerated. bun test 2839 pass / 0 fail (+29); typecheck, audit:registry (84 pages), check:bindings, check:skill, check:registry-index, check:schema-refs, check:audit-browser, check:docs (291 files) all green. No new dependencies.

stack 2.0 — the full flexbox surface, declared. Six attributes and three value sets that stack.css had always shipped were invisible to every manifest-driven surface; all are now declared. Direction is the design decision: it rode `data-variant`, which the tier grammar may not suffix (P1, frozen), so `data-direction` becomes canonical and responsive while `data-variant="horizontal"` stays as a deprecated 0.x alias selecting literally the same declaration block (asserted as one block, not merely the same outcome) — recorded as a `breaking: true` 2.0.0 changelog entry for 1.0-03 to pick up. gap (now 0..16), align (now incl. baseline), justify and direction are responsive variant groups; wrap, align-text, child flex and the deprecated `responsive` land under `props`. The bespoke `[data-responsive]` max-width collapse is re-expressed mobile-first on the canon and kept working as an alias, with `:where()` holding it at zero specificity so an explicit tier always wins — the sheet is now 4 ascending min-width blocks and zero max-width. 0.7-20's boolean-switch question answered: NOT a state (runtime vocabulary; data-wrap is authored and static) and NOT a variant (a closed value set with a default; data-wrap is valueless presence and would have had to become data-wrap="wrap", breaking every page writing it bare) — `props`, schema-formal since 0.8-02. One generic generator consequence: a boolean prop declaring an explicit `attr` now emits the presence shape a state does in src/bindings/ir.ts, so LStack gains `wrap?: boolean` with no emitter/runtime/spec-shape change and zero churn elsewhere (no other boolean prop in the registry declares an attr). Tests (tests/primitives/stack.test.ts, 26): completeness BOTH ways (nothing selected-but-undeclared, nothing declared-but-unselected) as the per-component forerunner of 0.8-10; a real cascade resolver over the parsed sheet — specificity, then document order, media filtered through a matchMedia mock — proving direction flips at md, tiers hand over to each other, gap tiers override mobile-first, and both deprecated spellings still resolve; and the generated surfaces (IR tier expansion, both committed LStack modules, the docs Responsive column, and the ABSENCE of `flex-wrap` in all twelve theme frames — the 0.7-20 payoff). bun test 2810 pass / 0 fail (+26); typecheck, check:bindings (zero drift), check:skill, check:registry-index, check:schema-refs, check:audit-browser, check:docs (291 files), audit:registry all green. Deliberately unchanged: stack.html renders pixel-identically (attribute rename only), so the four committed visual baselines stay valid.

Manifest schema gains `props` and `responsive`, and the category vocabulary closes. `props` was de-facto — 134 entries across 59 manifests, read by recipe-ir/icons, absent from the published schema; it is now a `prop` definition (type ∈ string|boolean|number|enum + description required; default/attr/values optional) derived from the shapes actually shipped, plus `ManifestProp`/`Manifest.props` in TS, which let recipe-ir.ts delete the local cast it used to reach a field the type system didn't know. `variant.responsive: true` means every declared value is also accepted as `data-<attr>-<tier>` for the 0.8-01 canon tiers, and FOUR surfaces consume that one declaration generically: bindings expand `cols` → `colsSm/colsMd/colsLg/colsXl` (ir.ts for primitives; a post-pass over the finished render tree in recipe-ir.ts for recipes, so both registration paths share one implementation), with tier props REUSING the base group's union — one exported type per group, not one per prop; the docs variant matrix grows a Responsive column; the skill grows the column plus a canon-quoting grammar line; context gains `responsive: {attr:[tiers]}` and the markdown/llms-full surfaces a `Responsive:` line from one formatter. Every surface is tested in both directions — a component declaring nothing gains no column/key/line — which is why 82 docs pages, the committed skill and the bindings stayed byte-identical (check:bindings zero drift) even though the generators changed. `valid-variant` learns the suffix grammar: wrong value and unknown tier are separate findings, reported independently, and a suffixed attribute of a NON-responsive group is deliberately ignored (0.8-10's rule, not this one's). No registry component declares a responsive group yet — 0.8-03/0.8-04 are first — so the contract is proven against probe manifests and a scratch-registry probe recipe BEFORE the CSS lands, not after. Category: `form`(3)→`forms`(17), `marketing`(4) documented, closed 11-value enum shared by schema + MANIFEST_CATEGORIES + CONTRIBUTING, with a drift test that parses the vocabulary back out of CONTRIBUTING's prose; `custom` is in the enum for `faqir create` and excluded from the registry by test. bun run test 2784 pass / 0 fail (+33); typecheck, check:bindings, check:skill, check:registry-index, check:audit-browser, check:schema-refs (95), check:docs (291 files), audit:registry all green.

Docs site agent surfaces + hosting artifacts. Four machine files at stable root URLs (llms.txt, llms-full.txt, manifest.schema.json, registry-index.json) plus _headers and one copy-for-agents payload per component. The llms pair is the CLI's OWN generator pointed at the registry, not a second rendering: generateContext was split into a pure composeContextData and src/generator/registry-context.ts feeds it every registry manifest; the site's files are asserted byte-equal to formatContextLlms/formatContextLlmsFull over that data. Two forced changes: meta.scope (a hosted file may not say 'this project installs …') and entries passed as [name,manifest] PAIRS instead of a Map, because empty-state ships in two layers and a name-keyed map drops one. Paths are the contract: tests/generator/docs-agents.test.ts spells every agent-facing path out as a LITERAL (deriving them from the generator's constants would only assert self-agreement) and a second case pins the constants to those literals. Schema + index copied byte-identical from the repo; schema served at the path its own $id claims (parsed, compared) and re-validated through the hosted bytes against all 83 manifests; index checked for faqir-registry-index@1, matching count, full coverage and a 64-hex hash per file. _headers is generated from the same list that emits the files, so nothing is served without a content type + CORS. Copy for agents: 83 standalone documents — reference fragment verbatim under the two-tag CDN preamble, EXACT version pin with matching SRI — asserted as documents in happy-dom (parses, exactly one link + one script both matching packages/core/cdn.json, no range pin, nothing relative, fragment byte-for-byte) and clean under DOCUMENT_RULES, inherited structurally because payload and example page mount through one mountFragment. The payload is three things from one source (visible <pre><code>, the file, the clipboard): the button copies textContent of the block it names, and the test clicks it in a DOM and compares the clipboard string to the snippet file, binding navigator explicitly to the window so it cannot pass against the test runner's. .html.txt not .html is deliberate — a payload, not a page — so 'no page the site serves reaches the network' stays absolute and no page class, audit gate, axe sweep or link rule needed an exception. SRI needed a hermetic source since packages/core/dist is git-ignored and absent in CI: build:core-package now also writes the COMMITTED packages/core/cdn.json, and the contract test fails while its version disagrees with packages/core/package.json. Checked and stated plainly: @faqir-ui/core is NOT published to npm yet, so the pinned URLs go live with 1.0-04. Deploy: bun run deploy:site (build:docs then `wrangler pages deploy`, no args — wrangler.toml carries name + pages_build_output_dir); wrangler via bunx, no new dependency; deployment stays a human step. Filed 0.7-21 (two `### empty-state` blocks in llms-full.txt share one anchor, so the pattern is unreachable by link). bun test 2735 pass / 0 fail (+28); check:docs 291 files / 4.25 MB; typecheck, check:audit-browser, check:skill, check:schema-refs, check:registry-index, audit:registry green; a11y 541 pass with only the four pre-existing tag-input failures of 0.7-16.

Docs site: in-browser audit playground + theme gallery — the audit engine now runs CLIENT-SIDE with no server, and every theme is one swappable <link> away. To make the engine bundlable at all, auditHtmlSource moved to the new src/audit/html-audit.ts, whose entire import graph is free of node:* (checker.ts keeps node:fs for the on-disk sweep and re-exports the core, so there is still exactly ONE implementation and CLI↔browser parity is STRUCTURAL rather than re-implemented). scripts/build-audit-browser.mjs compiles src/audit/browser.ts to site/lib/faqir-audit.js — an IIFE installing one global, 28.76 KB raw / 9.76 KB gzip — COMMITTED like registry/core/faqir-core.js because the docs generator is pure/node:fs-only and copies files rather than invoking a bundler; `check:audit-browser` is its drift gate (CI + spawned from bun test) and it BIT twice during the session. Client-side proven three ways: the bundle audits inside a bare node:vm context with no DOM/require/module loader; it contains no node: specifier, no bundler runtime, no fetch/XHR/dynamic import and no http URL; and in Chromium against the served site every request is recorded and NOTHING leaves the origin. Manifests ship as a <script> assigning one global (311.67 KB, the whole registry verbatim — trimming would make parity a property of the serializer instead of the engine), so even file:// works. Parity: 513 shared fixtures (every site page, every reference fragment raw+sanitized, 150 fuzz-corpus samples, 14 dirty snippets) compared deep-equal, skipRules included, plus an assertion that the engine's audit-error fallback never fires. The one browser-only concern is manifest keying and it bit: empty-state ships as BOTH a primitive and a pattern, runAudit lets the last layer loaded win, so a first draft that sorted the payload keys audited those components against the wrong contract (27 fixtures disagreed) — payload is now written in load order, manifestMap does not re-sort, both halves regression-tested. Theme gallery: 12 themes (discovered, not listed), each with its own stylesheet, its own preview frame and a card described from its .theme.json; light+dark+auto. Instant switching asserted in Chromium by COMPUTED COLOUR: a scheme click flips data-theme on <html> and bg+fg both change; a theme click rewrites the href of one <link id=faqir-theme> and the page restyles into it; a value stashed on window survives both, proving no navigation. Scheme reaches all 12 frames at once by postMessage (frames are told, never reached into — file:// has no same-origin access to its own frames). That required splitting the stylesheet: styles/faqir.css is tokens+base+components and the theme is a SECOND link every page of the site carries, so the switcher is the site's own mechanism. The theme therefore loads one step later than faqir init concatenates it — safe in both directions and asserted, not assumed: no component CSS declares :root, and contrast.css (the only theme targeting components) already outranks them on specificity. One frame document per theme rather than ?theme=, so the theme is right before first paint (tested with all JS blocked) and every URL stays a relative path the link checker resolves. Third LAYOUT, not a third gate: frames/** are site pages under the same 100%-audit-clean + axe-clean gate (isShellPage / isFramePage name the layouts, isSitePage still names the gate) — and that gate bit HARD. Rendering a component in all 12 themes for the first time produced 15 axe contrast failures on badge's soft variants; reproduced statically with the framework's own checkThemeContrast (10 of 12 themes, 1.96:1 → 4.50:1), root-caused to CONTRAST_TOKENS_RULE exempting the -subtle feedback pairs on the false premise that they carry no text, filed as 0.7-19 (with the baseline-regeneration caveat), and the frame now shows solid component colour + bare token swatches until it lands. Also filed 0.7-20: stack ships data-wrap in CSS but never declares it in its manifest, so nothing manifest-derived (docs site, skill, context, bindings) knows the attribute exists and no rule catches the gap — the frames wrap with an inline flex-wrap instead. Site JS is a closed named list on exactly three pages (playground, gallery, frame); all 83 component pages, the index, the token reference and the home page are still static HTML + stylesheets, held there by a test. Findings are built with createElement/textContent, never innerHTML; the preview frame is sandbox=allow-scripts (no allow-same-origin) so recipe controllers run but cannot reach the page. 45 new bun tests + 30 new axe pages; full suite 2707 pass / 0 fail (+45); build:docs 201 files / 3.22 MB, check:docs and check:audit-browser clean; typecheck, audit:registry, size, bindings, registry-index, skill and schema-ref gates green; docs-site axe gate 201/201 and the full a11y suite 539 pass with only the 4 pre-existing tag-input failures of 0.7-16. No new dependencies.

Docs site scaffold — site/ is a Faqir project with NO build step at runtime and only ONE hand-written page fragment (site/content/home.html) plus five strings in site.config.json; everything else is derived from manifests by the pure, node:fs-only generator src/generator/docs.ts (runs identically under bun test, the Playwright/Node runner, and scripts/build-docs.mjs). `bun run build:docs` → 171 files / 2.61 MB: 86 site pages (home, component index, token reference, 83 component pages), 83 live-example pages, one stylesheet (tokens+base+theme+every component CSS, the faqir init cascade order), one engine copy. Shell = the dashboard-shell pattern; content = [data-ui=prose]; nav/link/badge/card/grid/separator/text/callout are the only other components — zero class attributes, zero own CSS, zero own JS. Per-component pages carry: live example, anatomy tree + slot table, variant matrix (every declared value as the attribute an author types), states, a11y table, token list linked by anchor into the token reference, templates, transforms, two-way composition links. The load-bearing design decision: TWO page classes with different gates, documented in docs/docs-site.md. Site pages must be 100% auditHtmlSource-clean at EVERY severity (they are) and axe-clean (172 scans, 86 pages × light/dark, over real HTTP). examples/** wrap a registry reference fragment VERBATIM and are held to the document rules — the scope the registry self-audit already applies to that markup — plus controller-loaded, the one per-component rule that judges the wrapper (which is why recipe examples are live: they load registry/core/faqir-core.js). That split is content-derived, not a per-component escape hatch, and two tests prove the ground: every example body IS its registry fragment byte-for-byte, and every example component IS in the 0.4-24 a11y matrix. Probed and rejected the alternatives first: neither the reference fragments (365 findings) nor instantiated manifest templates (27/83 dirty) are clean under the per-component rules — filed as 0.7-17, which also affects `faqir audit` in user projects. Landmark placement is derived from the fragment, never from a name: own-<main> mounts as-is, dialog-class markup mounts BESIDE <main>, everything else is wrapped. Both gates bit and changed the site: <pre tabindex=0> (scrollable-region-focusable) and no <code> inside <a> — prose's code plate is --color-bg-muted with no colour, so --color-primary lands at 4.41:1 in dark (filed as 0.7-18; links now use the text primitive's mono variant). Also found: a JS-flipped data-theme samples mid-transition and reports phantom contrast failures, so the spec freezes transitions before the swap; and the sidebar must NOT carry data-state=expanded or dashboard-shell's 768px off-canvas drawer parks 83 links on top of the content on a phone. Layer-scoped page paths because empty-state is both a primitive and a pattern (the first draft's name-keyed map silently dropped one — now a regression test). Verified in Chromium against the served site: the dialog opens live inside the docs page's iframe (data-state=open, real overlay + focus trap) and the accordion goes collapsed→expanded. 30 new bun tests + 173 axe cases; full suite 2662 pass / 0 fail (+30); typecheck, audit:registry, size, bindings, registry-index, skill and schema-ref gates green; the full a11y suite is green except the 4 pre-existing tag-input cases of 0.7-16, whose diagnosis this session corrected (the taglist is not empty — the role=combobox input inside role=list is the violation). No new dependencies.

Dev overlay + Faqir.inspect + faqir-core.dev.js — TWO engine builds from ONE source. scripts/build-core.mjs now emits registry/core/faqir-core.js AND faqir-core.dev.js, resolved by three markers (exported+unit-tested applyDevMarkers): `/* @faqir:dev */` drops a line for production, `// @faqir:dev-start`…`-end` drops a region, `// @faqir:dev-diagnostics` injects src/core-src/dev-diagnostics.js into the dev build only. Diagnostics reach the engine through ONE seam (`var devHooks = null`), so production carries neither the guards nor the messages; the byte-freeness gate DERIVES its string list from dev-diagnostics.js (comments stripped, literals ≥12 chars) instead of hand-listing, and runs against both the registry engine and the minified CDN artifact — plus `devReport`/`devSnippet`/`function isReorder` absent and exactly two surviving `devHooks` mentions. Warning-class policy made explicit: ERRORS stay in both builds (production terse, dev rich with the offending element's outerHTML), ADVISORIES are dev-only — so the unkeyed-l-for-reorder hint MOVED out of production along with its isReorder detector and per-update list snapshot (its three tests moved to the dev file; production kept parallel silence assertions), and two new advisories landed (unknown-directive, l-html unsanitized notice, each deduped per element). Faqir.inspect(el|selector) → { el, scopeRoot, scopeId, scope, directives, controller, state } SHIPS IN PRODUCTION (it is the agent surface; 1.0-02 types it): `scope` is a plain deep copy — magics excluded because they are non-enumerable by construction, functions/elements/cycles/depth collapse to markers, and reading registers NO reactive dependency; `directives` normalized (arg:null, modifiers:[]); `controller.api` is the identical object the controller returned; `state` reads the five protocol attributes ui-scoped exactly as $state/$variant do. window.__FAQIR_DEVTOOLS__ (version 1; keys version/dev/faqir/inspect/scopes/components/stores/warnings) is installed by both builds and mirrored as Faqir.devtools — the shared-realm problem the suite surfaced: with two builds loadable in one process only an instance-bound name is deterministic, so the global's identity is pinned against a freshly evaluated faqir-core.min.js. The overlay lives in src/dev/overlay.ts, bundled into the CLI and deliberately NOT in the registry so `faqir init` cannot copy it and `faqir bundle --js` cannot bundle it (both asserted, plus a needle-grep over the whole registry tree and dist); `faqir dev` serves it at /__faqir/devtools.js and rewrites HTML responses on the way out (disk untouched; --no-overlay opts out), proven end-to-end against a real spawned server over node:http (happy-dom's fetch enforces same-origin and refuses). Shadow-rooted, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F toggles, Escape closes; renders scopes with live data, components with protocol attributes and their OWN parts, and diagnostics. Verified in real Chrome against a faqir init project: all four diagnostic classes fire, the overlay toggles and renders, and the project's production engine matches none of the dev strings while still installing the handle. Size: engine+controllers 42.35 → 43.08 KB gzip for inspect/devtools, gate 43 → 44 KB (same precedent as 0.7-06/0.7-07); the dev engine is a new report-only target (budgetBytes:null → checkBudget returns reportOnly, cannot fail enforce at any size) printed at 44.03 KB gzip, with build:core also reporting 346.96 KB raw dev vs 340.18 KB production. Docs: new docs/devtools.md, README, CONTRIBUTING (seam table), AGENTS.md, the faqir-creator skill's references/directives.md, and a new `devtools` block in the generated project context (context.json + Markdown + llms.txt index + llms-full.txt tables). 94 new tests; full suite 2632 pass / 0 fail (+94); typecheck, audit:registry, size, bindings, registry-index, skill and schema-ref gates green. No new dependencies.

Density mode — `[data-density="compact"|"comfortable"]` remaps the spacing scale and the control height ramp for a subtree, in ONE new file (registry/tokens/density.css, two rule blocks) with zero JS (build:core untouched at 29 controllers) and no sixth protocol attribute. The load-bearing CSS fact, documented in the file header and enforced by tests: a var() inside a custom property is substituted where the property is DECLARED, so a single :root multiplier cannot work — each density block re-declares --space-1…--space-24 as calc(base * var(--density-scale)) (scale 0.75; --space-0/--space-px invariant), plus an EXPLICIT control ramp 28/32/40 rather than the multiplier (40×0.75=30px is below a usable hit target), plus every :root alias whose value reads a remapped token (--card-padding, --field-gap, --callout-padding-*, --kv-*-gap, --button-height-*, --input-height) re-declared verbatim so it re-substitutes in scope. That dependent set is DERIVED from aliases.css+doc-aliases.css by a drift test, not hand-listed. document.css (--doc-*/--page-*) deliberately excluded: print density is a theme concern. Extension the task implied but the registry lacked: --control-height-{sm,md,lg} is now the canonical ramp in aliases.css with button/input aliasing it — surface grew by 3, so all 12 theme manifests regenerated; density.css itself is excluded from the themeable surface via a new shared isSurfaceTokenFile (replacing a copy-pasted `!== index.css` filter in 4 places) because a theme's :root cannot reach a subtree scope. Scoping proven in happy-dom by reading tokens the way a component does (a probe rule consuming them), since happy-dom does not expose inherited custom properties directly: descendants at any depth and the density element itself tighten, a sibling subtree does not, inner comfortable resets, compact-in-comfortable-in-compact still tightens, an unknown value is inert. Found en route: @faqir-ui/forms has emitted data-density from opts.density since 0.6-03 with no CSS behind it — now resolves, pinned by two tests; the generator stays outside the no-JS grep (it writes markup a human could type). New reference page registry/tokens/density.html (same form+table authored at both densities + a nesting block), deliberately NOT @ui:component so it stays out of the 84×12 matrix; captured by its own spec over default/slate/soft × {light,dark}, each capture first asserting IN PAGE that the compact button resolved shorter (a screenshot cannot go green on an inert attribute), and axe-scanned on the component gate's axes ({default,contrast}×{light,dark}, 4 scans, zero violations/exemptions). Caught in Chrome: the page used data-direction=horizontal on stack; the real variant is data-variant. Documented for agents in context.json (new `density` block + both prose renderers + the llms.txt index), the skill's references/tokens.md, and README. 31 new tests; full suite 2538 pass / 0 fail (+31); typecheck, audit:registry, size, bindings, registry-index, skill and schema-ref gates green; verified through a real faqir init in both concatenated and --tokens-split modes and in the CDN bundle.

Themes terminal + glass + soft — theme count 9→12 (plan said 'reaches 10'; document-serif had already landed out-of-band, noted as drift). All three are full 32-token themes (27 colors + 5 shadows) in :root/[data-theme=dark]/auto blocks. terminal: phosphor green (oklch hue 145, C≥0.21) on near-black with amber warnings, glow shadows instead of depth, --font-sans aliased to var(--font-mono) so the whole UI is monospaced, every radius token AND component radius alias zeroed; dark-primary declared honestly — scheme:both backed by a real 'paper terminal' light scheme (dark-green ink on green-tinted paper), moods dark/terminal/technical/mono/retro. glass: authored fallback-first — every token solid, and ALL translucency (color-mix + backdrop-filter) lives inside one @supports ((-webkit-backdrop-filter…) or (backdrop-filter…)) block that frosts --card-bg / --glass-panel (color-mix over var(--color-bg…), so one declaration follows both schemes) and applies blur to card/dialog-panel/sheet-panel/popover-content/toast via :root-boosted selectors (recipes hardcode background:var(--color-bg) at equal specificity). glass.test.ts documents and enforces the translucent-contrast computation: color-mix(C p%, transparent) ≡ C at α=p/100 (premultiplied), composited channel-wise in gamma-encoded sRGB over EVERY opaque theme surface (bg/bg-subtle/bg-muted), fg+fg-muted ≥ AA per scheme; plus the stripped fallback must clear the full standard pair list with every pair actually computed (no silent translucent skips), and comments are stripped before the structural assertions (a first-run bug: prose mentioning @supports ate the light block). soft: pastel consumer/health — warm cream/cocoa surfaces, calm low-chroma teal primary (C≤0.12 is what reads as pastel; inks stay deep for AA), pill buttons/badges via radius-full, 1rem/1.5rem/2rem radius scale; moods pastel/friendly/consumer/health/calm/rounded, test-enforced fully disjoint from terminal's (the acceptance criterion). One contrast fix en route: glass dark destructive 0.60→0.58 L (white label was 4.39:1). All gates are glob-driven — coverage matrix, manifest consistency, contrast-tokens AA, and the visual matrix picked the three up with zero edits; 12-capture Playwright smoke green; all three previews (aurora-derived; glass gets radial-gradient blobs behind the panels so the frost is visible) browser-verified in both schemes. Manifests generated via SEED entries + gen:theme-manifests, $schema via gen:schema-refs. 71 new tests; full suite 2507 pass / 0 fail (+71); typecheck + audit:registry green. No JS, no size/bindings/skill cascade — themes are CSS+manifest only.

Patterns stats-dashboard + inbox — two composition-only patterns with ZERO JavaScript of their own (no controller file; build:core untouched at 29 controllers). stats-dashboard is a reporting page: the KPI row IS data-ui=grid (data-cols=4/data-cols-md=2), so 4->2->1 is grid.css and the pattern's sheet declares no metrics columns at all — the deliberate trade being that the stats inside carry no data-part (it would be an orphan part of the grid); report panels are cards; the report table is the table recipe with its full formatting contract (data-format on th repeated on every td, raw data-value, tfoot data-aggregate/data-col) and a test that adds up each aggregated column and compares it with the AUTHORED total. Corrected against table.js en route: aggregation is declared in the tfoot alone — a footer cell reads a whole column by index, body cells opt into nothing (the first draft's data-aggregate on body cells was removed from markup and manifest). Slot named `report` not `panel` because the audit's aria-describedby rule treats [data-part=panel] as a dialog's describable surface. inbox is a fully declarative list-detail view: two instances of the same markup on one page — authored rows, and l-source:messages + <template l-for l-key> for rows AND details — with selection in one l-data and everything else bound (:hidden, :data-state, :aria-current, l-text, @click); a directive-vocabulary test pins exactly which directives the page may use. Both instances are driven under real faqir-core with fetch stubbed: selection swaps the pane, aria-current + data-state mark the open row, back clears it, empty state renders when nothing is selected, the served JSON renders two rows/details, and a 503 surfaces the role=alert error line. Deviation: the reactive :data-state sits on the PANES, not the root, because faqir-core never applies bind directives on an l-data scope root (known follow-up 0.6-15) — the collapse CSS keys on [data-part=…-pane][data-state=inactive] and the manifest says why. Responsive collapse is pure CSS at the registry's 640px breakpoint, tested through a matchMedia mock that reads the real rules out of inbox.css. Breakpoint canon + responsive doctrine. ONE ladder (sm 40rem/640 · md 48rem/768 · lg 64rem/1024 · xl 80rem/1280), min-width-only, replacing three incompatible ones (grid's 640/641-1024 viewport ranges with a real 640.5px dead zone, table's 480/768/1024 container thresholds where sm meant a different number, surface's 640-1400 max-widths). Canon lives in src/utils/breakpoints.ts because media queries cannot read custom properties, so the numbers must be literal in CSS and can only be kept honest by one module that generators, tests and (0.8-10) the audit all read; it is node:*-free so the browser audit bundle can import it. Frozen exports + helpers that structurally cannot emit max-width, and a data-<attr>-<tier> grammar that refuses the five protocol attributes in BOTH directions (responsiveAttribute throws, parseResponsiveAttribute returns null) so data-size-md is unreachable rather than discouraged. FAQIR-SPEC.md gains §15 (ladder table, five rules, grammar, doctrine) and FAQIR-NEXT.md §19 (why layout is agent-critical: ten layout attributes no manifest declares; the intrinsic -> container -> viewport hierarchy; what v0.8 ships) + Decision Summary item 13. The spec is executable documentation: a drift test re-parses the canon table and compares rem and px to the module, §15's CSS fences must use canon min-width only, and its HTML fences pass auditHtmlSource against every registry manifest. The 0.7-08/0.7-09 pattern guards now source 640/1024 from BREAKPOINTS instead of inline literals, keeping the legacy max-width form until 0.8-09 flips it. No registry file touched.
